skill.name: nature-image2ppt
skill.description: Reconstruct slide images, screenshots, scanned PDFs, and image-only presentations as editable PowerPoint objects with layout preservation, speaker notes, and rendered quality checks.
skill.summary: Rebuild existing visual slides as editable PowerPoint files with structured objects and quality checks.
skill.author: yuan1z0825

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives from PowerPoint XML, Markdown backticks, defensive path tests, and fixed argument-list subprocess calls. Confirmed risks include credential access, external image and OCR transfers, plaintext secret configuration, and optional TeX shell escape. Semantic review also found automatic Codex token reuse, an unvalidated OCR result URL, and misleading cloud-consent language. Static review was capped at 400/784 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 384 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The image backend automatically reuses a local Codex OAuth token.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before reading the auth file or sending each task to an external image service. Display the exact destination and files.

remediation.issue: The OCR result download accepts a service-provided URL without destination validation.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only HTTPS result URLs on approved PaddleOCR hosts. Disable redirects or validate every redirect, and enforce strict response-size limits.

remediation.issue: The OCR setup prompt calls third-party service use risk-free.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the claim and disclose that source pages leave the local machine. Request explicit approval for sensitive documents before upload.

remediation.issue: API keys and OCR tokens can be stored as plaintext YAML values.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables or an operating-system credential store. If YAML remains supported, warn users and retain owner-only permissions.

remediation.issue: Formula rendering can enable TeX shell escape.
remediation.suggestion: Remove shell-escape support or run TeX in a restricted sandbox with no network, minimal filesystem access, and a fixed engine path.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Reuse of Local Codex OAuth Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The image backend automatically reads a local Codex access token when present and sends it with slide prompts or images. Host allowlisting and redirect blocking limit exfiltration, but per-use consent is not required.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly reads access_token from the Codex auth file, adds it as a bearer header, and posts a body containing task data.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated OCR Result URL Enables SSRF
semantic_findings.description: The OCR client fetches a result URL supplied by the remote service without restricting its scheme, host, or redirects. A compromised response could make the client contact an unintended internal or external address.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The polling response controls status.resultUrl.jsonUrl, which is passed directly to requests.get without destination validation.

semantic_findings.title: Misleading Cloud OCR Consent Language
semantic_findings.description: The runtime describes a third-party OCR quota as risk-free and asks users to configure a token. This language omits document-upload privacy risks and may weaken informed consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The message explicitly claims the service is risk-free with no extra cost while encouraging token setup before reconstruction.

content.user_title: Rebuild Slide Images as Editable PowerPoint
content.value_statement: Flat slide images are difficult to revise or reuse. This skill reconstructs them as editable PowerPoint objects and validates the rendered result.
actual_capabilities: Accepts slide images, screenshots, scanned PDFs, and image-only PPT or PPTX inputs.
Reconstructs text, shapes, circles, connectors, arrows, formulas, and bounded image assets.
Uses semantic regions to rebuild flowcharts, knowledge graphs, and compound diagrams.
Preserves speaker notes from supported PowerPoint inputs during final assembly.
Creates page manifests, editable PPTX files, previews, contact sheets, and quality reports.
Validates page structure, path confinement, visual evidence, arrow integrity, and final rendering.
limitations: It reconstructs existing slides and does not author a new presentation from notes.
Complex illustrations may remain as replaceable bitmap assets when native reconstruction would reduce fidelity.
Cloud image and OCR backends can transmit source material and require suitable credentials.
Reliable output depends on local fonts, rendering tools, and optional formula converters.

use_cases.title: Recover Editable Training Slides
use_cases.description: Convert archived screenshots into editable slides while preserving layouts, diagrams, and review evidence.

use_cases.title: Restore Scanned Research Decks
use_cases.description: Turn scanned PDF pages into structured PowerPoint slides with measured text and bounded visual assets.

use_cases.title: Modernize Image-Only Presentations
use_cases.description: Rebuild image-based PPTX files so design teams can update text, shapes, arrows, and speaker notes.

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild One Slide
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconstruct this slide image as an editable PowerPoint. Preserve the original layout, text, colors, and object positions. Complete rendered quality checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single slide image

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Scanned PDF
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this scanned PDF into an editable PPTX. Preserve page dimensions and visual structure. Keep complex illustrations as separate replaceable assets when necessary.

prompt_templates.title: Restore an Image-Only Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Rebuild this image-only presentation as editable slides. Preserve speaker notes, native arrows, connectors, formulas, and page order. Report remaining bitmap assets.

prompt_templates.title: Reconstruct Complex Diagrams
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconstruct these slides with measured semantic regions. Keep nodes, connectors, and simple shapes native. Use approved cloud services only after confirming data handling.

output_examples.input: A screenshot containing a title, three process cards, and connecting arrows.
output_examples.output: An editable PowerPoint slide with native text boxes, cards, connectors, arrowheads, a preview, and completed quality evidence.

output_examples.input: A scanned PDF with six lecture slides and mathematical formulas.
output_examples.output: A six-slide PPTX with reconstructed text, rendered formula assets, page manifests, visual previews, and final validation results.

output_examples.input: An image-only PPTX containing speaker notes and a complex knowledge graph.
output_examples.output: A rebuilt deck with preserved notes, native graph nodes and connectors, bounded complex assets, and a report listing remaining bitmaps.

best_practices: Provide the highest-resolution source available and specify required page ranges, fonts, or dimensions.
Choose offline processing for sensitive material, or approve each external service after reviewing its data destination.
Inspect rendered comparisons and remaining bitmap assets before accepting the final deck.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to create a new presentation from an outline or meeting notes.
Do not provide confidential slides to cloud backends without explicit authorization and suitable data-handling terms.
Do not treat a passing structural check as proof that the rendered slide matches the source.

faq.question: What input formats are supported?
faq.answer: The skill accepts slide images, screenshots, scanned PDFs, PPT files, and image-only PPTX files.

faq.question: Will every element become editable?
faq.answer: Text, simple shapes, arrows, and connectors can become native objects. Complex local illustrations may remain replaceable bitmap assets.

faq.question: Does it preserve speaker notes?
faq.answer: It preserves speaker notes from supported PowerPoint inputs and verifies note integrity during final validation.

faq.question: Can it work without cloud services?
faq.answer: Yes. Offline text geometry is available, but character recognition and image editing may be less complete without cloud backends.

faq.question: What files does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces an editable PPTX, page manifests, previews, contact sheets, validation results, and rendered quality reports.

faq.question: Is it suitable for confidential presentations?
faq.answer: Use offline processing for confidential material. Cloud image or OCR features can transmit slide content to external providers.
